patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Saleor share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose BigCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($2” rather than Saleor's shape. Choose Saleor only if your buying job matches “Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, En” rather than BigCommerce's shape. Workflow advantage: BigCommerce leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Saleor leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Saleor share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: BigCommerce is Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($299); GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees; Saleor is Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, Enterprise quote. Forever Free is non-commercial onl.
- Company-size focus: BigCommerce (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Saleor (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: BigCommerce-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b vs Saleor-leaning —.
- Researched limits: BigCommerce — 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Saleor — Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO.

Limitations — BigCommerce: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Native POS/retail depth trails Shopify/Square for omnichannel-first merchants; Saleor: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO; Forever Free Cloud is non-commercial — not a production merchant free plan.

Poor-fit cases: BigCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription · Saleor is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO · Avoid BigCommerce if you actually need Saleor's motion (Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
